measured_why: 75.2% of 2178 real fix pieces from 500 real SWE-bench Verified tasks are rebuilt by no operator any other task's fixes ever produced
with every other task's fixes as experience -- the asymptote, not a sample -- coverage is 18.7%
the largest expressible real edit is `delete` (348 pieces, 16.0% of all): a structural removal, and the grammar has can_delete_a_node=False
on real bugs classified by required edit shape, in-grammar types repair at 74.0% and out-of-grammar types at 32.0% (a 42.0 point separation that no amount of experience closes)
a new environment costs 29 trials to adapt and only pays back after 25.8 requests in it, so it is a change of currency (requests -> environments), not a free lunch
answers.the_single_bottleneck: REACH: the set of edits the proposer can name. Search, verification, memory and environment adaptation are all measured and bounded; reach is the term that sets the ceiling, and it is grown by deriving an edit from the failure witness (the test's own expected value at a localised site), never by enumerating more operator families by hand
what_is_false: that experience is the limiting term -- reach is, and experience does not move it
that competence follows from consequence knowledge: knowing what an action does is silent about which action to take when the needed action has no name in the vocabulary
that more experience per environment makes it permanent -- permamence holds only where survivors agree, and environment adaptation pays back only after the measured crossover
that the benchmark is a frontier measure -- SWE-bench Verified was retired in Feb 2026 because frontier models reproduce its gold patches from memory
what_is_true: one execution plus a computed sufficiency verdict is enough to know an action's consequence, where the survivors agree
instant learning in a new environment is real and is a cost law: adapt once, then plan
verification by execution is exact and cheap, and it is the reason anything here can be trusted
search over a fixed grammar is effective exactly on the defects inside that grammar

grammar_membership_predicts_repair.law: P(repair | defect type) is predicted by whether the edit the fix requires is a shape the grammar can name -- not by the amount of experience, and not by the quality of the search. The search does not fail on out-of-grammar defects; it exhausts and correctly reports OPEN

recomputation_vs_recording.reading: the difference is the pieces whose operator exists only inside their own task, which a leave-one-out view cannot hand them; the recomputation agreeing to this size is what makes the asymptote a measurement rather than an assumption

law: P(correct action) = REACH x SEARCH x VERIFICATION; experience moves REACH only by naming new actions, and it names none

real_fixes.meaning: N means no experience of any other task produces this piece of this fix. `delete` and `insert` are structural: they are not a value or an operator being wrong, so no amount of watching values and operators change can name them

what_this_shows: Measured over 500 real SWE-bench Verified tasks and 2178 real fix pieces, experience does not buy reach: 75.2% of pieces are rebuilt by no operator any other task ever produced, and with every other task's fixes as experience the coverage is 18.7% -- an asymptote, not a sample. The same wall appears from the other side on 100 real HumanEvalFix bugs: in-grammar defect types repair at 74.0%, out-of-grammar types at 32.0%, and the split is exactly whether the required edit is a shape the grammar can name. So the limiting term is REACH, not search, not verification, not memory: consequence knowledge is silent about which action to take when the needed action has no name yet. New environments do not change this -- they cost 29 trials to adapt and pay back only after 25.8 requests.
